I couldn't use `read_thread`, which is unavailable in this snapshot. Everything below comes from the source and from REQUEST.md. **What the snapshot already has.** The nested proposal is in place. `BufferSnapshot` has the states `unread | loading | unavailable | ready`, and a ready buffer carries `unsaved?: Unsaved` (`packages/folder/src/edit-owner.ts:123-145`). All the callers read `buffer.unsaved`. Five things in the code shape the answer: - **Typing during a save keeps the status `saving`, even though the text is now newer than what is being written** (`edit-owner.ts:1152`). So `saving` already coexists with newer, unsaved text. - **A retry clears the earlier error as soon as it starts** (`:847`). Typing clears a failure but keeps a conflict (`:1153-1155`). - **When a file is deleted elsewhere and there's no unsaved input, the text disappears** (`shownText`, `:1093-1099`). `FileEditor.svelte:55-64` works around this with `lastShown`. - **`discard()` is refused while a save is running** (`:1013-1016`). - **Every caller shows `dirty` and `saving` the same way, as "Saving…"** (`FileEditor.svelte:81`, `TextDetail.svelte:157-161`, `FileDetail.svelte:237-242`). None of them distinguishes the two. ## Answer to the central question **No.** Those five statuses shouldn't be one mutually exclusive value, because `saving` isn't the same kind of fact as the others. Four of them describe **how the editor's text relates to storage, and who has to act next**. `saving` describes **an operation in progress**, and the text it's writing may be older than the current text. It can run alongside `dirty` (typing during a save) and alongside `failed` (a retry). So your hypothesis holds: keeping `saving` in the union squashes two facts into a display priority. With `saving` taken out, the remaining relation *is* exclusive. Each value decides who makes progress and which command does it: > **status: `clean`** (nothing to write) · **`dirty`** (autosave will write it) · **`failed`** (this exact text was tried and failed; it waits for `save()`) · **`conflict`** (storage moved away from the base; it waits for `resolve()`) · **`detached`** (clean, but storage no longer holds text) **Errors attach to what they describe:** - A save failure is about one attempt, at one revision. It stops applying once the text changes. - A conflict is about the base, meaning the stored content the edits started from. It survives typing, because any later save from the same base would conflict too. - A read error is about what we know of storage. It never changes the text. ## Definitions - **revision**: a counter that goes up each time input is accepted. - **base**: the exact stored content the text last agreed with. That's either the first content read or the last save that landed. Every write is guarded against it (compare-and-swap). - **expected**: what storage will hold if every write in flight lands. That's the text of the attempt in flight, or the base if nothing is in flight. - **dirty**: the text differs from *expected*. - **saved (for revision r)**: a guarded write of r's text landed. - **`save()`**: write the revision that's current when you call it. It resolves `Ok({ revision })` once that revision or a later one has landed, so `revision` is at least the one you called with. Otherwise it resolves with the failure or conflict that stopped it. It also re-attempts a `failed` draft. - **`folder.flush()`**: skip the autosave pause everywhere, try every held draft that isn't in conflict once, and resolve with what is still unwritten (`{ path, text, revision, status, error }`). Closing the folder is a flush followed by refusing new input. - **conflict is detected as soon as it's known**: by a read, not only by a save. If storage differs from the base while there's local work, that's a conflict right away. ## Proposed API ```ts const opened = await folder.open('notes/a.md', { schema: Note }); if (opened.error) return show(opened.error); // Missing | NotText | ReadFailed using editor = opened.data; // released when the scope ends; held drafts stay with the folder editor.text; // always a string editor.markdown; // the same text, read through the schema editor.revision; editor.status; // { status:'clean' } | { status:'dirty' } // | { status:'failed'; error: SaveFailure } // | { status:'conflict'; theirs: FileContent | null } // | { status:'detached'; stored: 'missing' | 'not-text' } editor.saving; // { revision } | undefined (independent of status) editor.readError; // ReadError | undefined (independent; text unaffected) editor.locked; // reason | undefined (a fenced action holds the path) editor.replaceText(text); // Result; refusals are returned, never stored editor.change({ fields, body }); await editor.save(); editor.revert(); // text = base; returns the abandoned text await editor.resolve('theirs' | 'mine' | { text }); await editor.refresh(); ``` Svelte. The opener handles acquisition and release, so the editor component only ever sees text: ```svelte {#if opening.editor} {:else if opening.error?.name === 'Missing'}This note is no longer in the folder. {:else if opening.error}{opening.error.message} {:else}{/if} ``` ```svelte {#if s.status === 'failed'}Not saved: {s.error.message}{#if editor.saving} · Retrying…{/if} {:else if s.status === 'conflict'}Changed elsewhere {:else if s.status === 'dirty' || editor.saving}Saving… {:else if s.status === 'detached'}Deleted elsewhere. This is the last text you saw. {:else}Saved{/if} {#if s.status === 'failed'}{/if} {#if s.status === 'conflict'} {/if} {#if editor.readError}

Couldn't refresh: {editor.readError.message}. Your text is kept.

{/if}
